description:
The last leg of the ADR-001 trust story (docs/development/
tuning-adr-001-trust-and-hash-semantics.md names introspection receipts as
the design direction; the applied-ledger work deliberately left
applied_verified unclaimable). After tuning application and data load,
introspect the live schema (SHOW CREATE TABLE / information_schema /
duckdb_constraints) per platform, compare against the ledger's executed DDL
intents, and emit a receipt into the .tuning.json companion. For tuned
ClickHouse runs the applied ledger also records session SETs, not just DDL
(benchbox/core/tuning/applied_ledger.py); introspection must corroborate
every ledgered entry of every kind, DDL and session-setting readback alike,
before validation_status upgrades to applied_verified. A run whose schema
matches while a session setting was ignored or reset must not receive
applied_verified. Mismatches (of either kind) downgrade with a diff list.
Introspection failure is non-fatal and leaves applied_unverified (never
blocks a run).

anti_patterns.dont: No screen-scraping of engine-specific DDL text where a structured catalog exists

deferrals.reason: Skipped during #4 to avoid conflict with the then-unmerged #1264 (same receipt components). #1264 now merged -> follow-up can add the verified-state chip/row.
deferrals.summary: Explorer receipt display of verified state (results-explorer/src)

deferrals.reason: A full duckdb --tuning tuned/sorting run cannot reach applied_verified: DuckDB renders SORTING as CREATE INDEX pre-load, then the loader CTAS sorted-ingestion (CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE AS SELECT ORDER BY) DROPS the index -> no catalog footprint survives. Soundness invariant working correctly. Fix: record the CTAS ORDER BY as a corroboratable footprint, or re-create the index post-load. Also: ClickHouse minting applied_verified needs its key DDL (CREATE TABLE phase) folded into the ledger.
deferrals.summary: Make DuckDB sorting verification-eligible (record a corroboratable footprint)

preserves.behavior: Introspection never fails or slows a run materially (bounded queries, non-fatal)
applied_verified is claimable ONLY via corroboration - never derived from the ledger alone

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/tuning/applied_ledger.py: entry kinds the receipts corroborate - extend
benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/tuning.py validate_session_cache_control: existing settings-readback pattern - reuse

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m benchbox.cli.main run --platform duckdb --benchmark tpch --scale 0.01 --tuning tuned --non-interactive --output /tmp/receipt-check
verifications.description: E2E tuned duckdb run reaches applied_verified with a receipt in the companion
verifications.expected: validation_status applied_verified; receipt lists corroborated intents

Reuses #1 vocab (not forked). Unit tests in test_introspection.py.

Both bounded (LIMIT, scoped to ledger_tables) + non-fatal (errored state, never raise).

work_units.evidence: test_introspection.py + test_duckdb_introspection.py (adapter-upgrades-to-verified-ONLY-via-corroboration; induced mismatch->applied_unverified+diff; absent; introspection-failure->applied_unverified) + test_clickhouse_introspection.py + test_applied_receipt_export.py. 44 introspection tests pass; 9297 broad suite pass; ruff/ty clean. Demonstrated real path: index persists -> applied_verified 2/2; mismatch -> applied_unverified.
